routes.description: Show that the cited facts about pain, pleasure, languishing, and horrendous evil do not provide comparative evidence for naturalism over theism because the naturalistic likelihood is not established, soul-building can raise their likelihood on theism, or skeptical theism prevents the required likelihood comparison.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if at least one global neutralizer defeats the comparative inference: the naturalistic prediction remains unsupported, a sufficiently developed soul-building account makes the data no less expected on theism, or epistemic limits leave the theistic likelihood unavailable for the claimed comparison.

motionBridge.description: Establish that the total cited suffering data do not warrant a comparative evidential preference for naturalism over theism.

centralBridges.description: Require adequate support for the claim that naturalism predicts the observed suffering facts better, rather than merely accommodating their possibility.
Explain how morally significant agency, virtue formation, nonhuman development, and eventual defeat of suffering can make the observed data compatible with theistic purposes.
Show that limited access to divine reasons or the total moral structure prevents a warranted estimate of the suffering data's probability on theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether the biological analogy and selected evolutionary background information support the asserted naturalistic expectations.
Address whether less harmful means, afterlife compensation, or the destructive effects of suffering undermine the proposed theistic purposes.

routes.description: Show that biologically oriented pain and pleasure, widespread sentient languishing, and horrendous evil are collectively more expected on morally indifferent naturalism than on theism, and that neither soul-building nor skeptical theism neutralizes that comparative evidential force.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by defending the comparative-likelihood standard, establishing a naturalistic advantage for the principal classes of suffering facts, and showing that soul-building and skeptical-theist replies neither predict the observed distribution nor erase the force of known evidence.

motionBridge.description: Establish that the total cited suffering data provide comparative evidential support for naturalism over theism.

centralBridges.description: Defend the principle that evidence favors the hypothesis on which the observed facts are less surprising, without requiring either hypothesis to entail them.
Establish a comparative naturalistic advantage for biologically oriented pain and pleasure, sentient languishing, and horrendous evil.
Show that soul-building does not adequately predict the scope, distribution, proportions, or destructive severity of the observed suffering.
Show that uncertainty about unknown divine reasons does not cancel known comparative reasons or prevent naturalism from assigning the data a higher likelihood.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify background knowledge without building the disputed suffering observations into it or requiring an independent complete naturalistic explanation.
Explain why less harmful means, divine resources, compensation, or possible afterlives do not by themselves justify or predict the observed harms.

sections.title: Comparative Likelihood and Naturalistic Prediction
sections.rationale: This issue fixes the governing evidential standard and whether analogical reasoning, evolutionary background knowledge, and comparative surprise adequately support a naturalistic likelihood advantage.

sections.title: Biological Orientation of Pain and Pleasure
sections.rationale: The orientation of pain and pleasure toward biological goals, and its apparent moral randomness, forms an independent evidential comparison that each side must explain under its hypothesis.

sections.title: Sentient Flourishing and Languishing
sections.rationale: The prevalence, distribution, and nonhuman scope of languishing test whether natural processes or theistic purposes better predict the observed proportions of sentient welfare.

sections.title: Horrendous Evil and Divine Prevention
sections.rationale: The severity, morally destructive effects, and apparent preventability of horrendous evil create a distinct comparison involving divine empathy, available alternatives, and indifferent natural processes.

sections.title: Scope and Necessity of Soul-Building
sections.rationale: Soul-building is a principal global neutralizer, so the debate must address its reach across humans and animals, the necessity of actual harms, freedom, afterlife defeat, and any claimed fine-tuning.

sections.title: Skeptical Theism and Unknown Reasons
sections.rationale: The final global issue is whether limited human access to divine reasons makes the theistic likelihood unknowable or whether known comparative evidence remains probative despite that uncertainty.
